# OpenAI Adds Verified Business Profiles and AI Agents to ChatGPT


By OpenTools Team


·


November 12, 2026


OpenAI launched Businesses in ChatGPT in beta, letting companies claim verified profiles, track engagement, and launch AI agents that answer customer questions. The move pushes ChatGPT toward becoming a consumer discovery and commerce layer.


## Businesses Get a Home Inside ChatGPT


[OpenAI](https://opentools.ai/organizations/openai) introduced **Businesses in ChatGPT** in beta on Tuesday, letting companies claim verified profiles and launch AI agents that answer questions from the chatbot's users,[Quartz](https://qz.com/openai-chatgpt-business-profiles-ai-agents-111126) reported. The company says **1.2 billion people use ChatGPT each week** — a massive audience that businesses can now reach directly inside the app.


Through a tool called **Business Hub** , companies can claim their organization, manage their information, and view insights on how people engage with them.[Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/technology/openai-lets-businesses-claim-chatgpt-profiles-adds-ai-agents-us-e-commerce-firms-2026-11-10/) confirmed the launch, noting that OpenAI is initially rolling out Business Agents to eligible e-commerce and online service businesses in the U.S.


## How Business Agents Work


After claiming a business, eligible organizations can build, test, and launch an agent. When a business appears in a model response, users can open its ChatGPT profile and, if an agent exists, start a conversation to ask follow-up questions about its offerings. The agent conversation is **labeled and separate** from the user's original ChatGPT conversation, and distinct from ChatGPT's independent answers, according to[OpenAI](https://openai.com/index/introducing-businesses-chatgpt/) .


Businesses can sponsor their agent and use it as the destination for ChatGPT Ads. Sponsored placements are labeled and kept separate from ChatGPT's own responses.[OpenAI](https://opentools.ai/organizations/openai) withholds users' conversations and agent chats from businesses — a privacy line that keeps the feature from becoming a surveillance tool.


## Insights: Mentions, Clicks, and Discovery Topics


Business Hub gives verified businesses **28 days of aggregated activity** , including **mentions, website clicks, and discovery topics** — the common themes in conversations where a business's website is cited. The insights appear only when conversations or interactions meet certain thresholds, per[Quartz](https://qz.com/openai-chatgpt-business-profiles-ai-agents-111126) .


[TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/10/openai-rolls-out-new-business-profiles-making-chatgpt-just-a-little-bit-more-like-google/) framed the launch as ChatGPT becoming "just a little bit more like[Google](https://opentools.ai/organizations/google) " — a consumer discovery engine where businesses control how they appear.[OpenAI](https://opentools.ai/organizations/openai) has given no details on its verification process beyond what VP of Monetization Benji Shomair told journalists Monday: "There are multiple verification methods that we use for different types of business in different markets,"[TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/10/openai-rolls-out-new-business-profiles-making-chatgpt-just-a-little-bit-more-like-google/) reported.


## The Shopify Connection


For e-commerce builders, the most concrete integration is **Shopify** . Shopify merchants can connect their store from Business Hub or directly from the Shopify admin, letting product data — including pricing and availability — flow into ChatGPT, according to[Quartz](https://qz.com/openai-chatgpt-business-profiles-ai-agents-111126) . Enterprise customers and advertisers can also work with an[OpenAI](https://opentools.ai/organizations/openai) representative to get set up.


This follows OpenAI's **September test of Sponsored Agents** , which let users who tapped an ad open a dialogue with an[AI agent](https://opentools.ai/tools/ai-agent) backed by the advertiser, involving select U.S. advertisers. OpenAI also retired an earlier ChatGPT shopping effort in March that used commission fees and a checkout cart — the new model is agentic conversation, not a cart.


## What This Means for Builders


The launch signals[OpenAI](https://opentools.ai/organizations/openai) 's bet that **AI agents will become the front door to commerce** . For developers and freelancers who build Shopify stores, e-commerce tools, or customer-facing services, Businesses in ChatGPT creates a new distribution surface: a verified profile and an agent that can answer customer questions without a human in the loop.


It's also a new SEO-like battleground. The *discovery topics* metric mirrors what[Google](https://opentools.ai/organizations/google) Search Console tells site owners about queries — except now it's about how often ChatGPT cites your business. For builders who understand both search and agentic AI, that's a wedge into a channel that's still early and uncompetitive.


The downside: Business Agents are currently limited to **eligible U.S. e-commerce and online service firms** , and OpenAI hasn't shared a public roadmap for broader access. OpenAI said it plans to extend the feature to more markets and categories and build tools for organizations with more complex needs.


## The Bigger Picture


- **1.2B weekly users** ChatGPT's reach is the draw — businesses can now appear directly in model responses to that audience


- **Agentic, not cart-based** OpenAI abandoned its March shopping cart; the new model is conversational agents answering questions


- **Shopify first** The Shopify integration gives merchants a plug-and-play path to a ChatGPT presence


- **U.S.-only for now** Business Agents start with eligible U.S. e-commerce and online service firms, with more markets promised
